label: late original-phase input j (weak, diffuse)
explanation: Diffuse unit. About 80% of activation mass falls in the original (input) phase, and the firing rate climbs with position (orig_idx 8 fires about 10x the base rate). It never fires at t=0 and almost never at the delimiter. The strongest single driver is input token j (42% of mass, 11.6x lift), and the top activations (around 0.9-1.0 of max) are almost all j inputs at original positions 6-8. Weaker drivers are inputs 2, c, h, u, v, n and 0, a preceding 0, and sequences with many digits. The remaining ~20% of mass is in the early copy phase (recall_idx 1-2) of long sequences. Magnitude is largest for j late in the original phase. However, a late j fires on only ~40% of occurrences, and most activations happen on non-j tokens, so no compact predicate does well. The best is (phase 0, input j, t>=4): dev F1 0.32, mass recall 0.35. Broader token-set or late-position predicates reach mass recall 0.6-0.8 but with precision 0.05-0.15. It does not fire on early original positions, the delimiter, or late copy steps.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by phase (input phase: j, c, 2, h; copy phase: v, 3, u, 2; delimiter step: ) and the previous input (most: 0, j, h, <DEL>, y, c; least: 3, p, q, -); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=2, recall_idx=1, L=8 & t=7.
